status_definitions.catalogue_verified: Official subject catalogue reviewed; this does not imply full syllabus, paper structure or grade rules have been ingested.
status_definitions.specification_verified: Specific official subject specification reviewed for the stated qualification and version.
status_definitions.historical_reference: Official historical source useful for context but not current requirements.

policy.answer_rule: Do not infer subject-specific paper structures, grade thresholds, equivalencies or current-year rules from a general landing page. Cite sources and state when details remain unverified.
policy.copyright_rule: Store concise factual notes and links; do not reproduce full syllabuses or copyrighted examination papers.
policy.grade_calculation_rule: Raw percentage is earned marks divided by maximum marks. Never convert raw percentages to board grades unless the exact official grading table matches board, qualification, subject and examination session.

sources.qualification: IGCSE, O Level, AS & A Level
sources.title: Our awarding standards
sources.summary: Official explanation of Cambridge grade-threshold setting and awarding standards.
verified_notes: Cambridge uses statistical evidence from current and previous comparable candidate groups and expert judgement about paper difficulty when setting grade thresholds.
The page states that grading decisions are made by experts and reviewed by a second expert team, rather than being decided automatically by a computer.
Evidence is considered for each qualification component because assessments can test different skills and have different candidate populations.
sources.limits: Not a subject syllabus and does not provide a universal fixed percentage for a grade. Check the exact qualification, component and examination series.

sources.title: About Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs
sources.summary: Official overview of Pearson Edexcel International GCSE.
verified_notes: Pearson describes International GCSE as an international qualification with content and assessment designed for international learners.
Pearson states that many International GCSE subjects offer a choice of linear or modular assessment; the applicable route must be checked for the individual subject.
sources.limits: Overview does not replace the current subject specification or grading documents.

sources.title: FBISE Syllabus and Model Question Papers
sources.publisher: Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
sources.summary: Official FBISE portal for syllabus, schemes, model papers and assessment resources.
verified_notes: The FBISE portal groups syllabus and model-question-paper resources under SSC and HSSC levels.
The portal states that it provides syllabus, scheme of studies, model papers and objective-type test items.
sources.limits: Identify class, subject, scheme/version and examination session before giving a detailed answer.

sources.title: WASSCE entry regulations
sources.summary: Official WAEC Nigeria page describing WASSCE entry regulations.
verified_notes: The current page describes a minimum of eight and maximum of nine subjects for the candidate cohort covered by the notice.
The page notes that Citizenship and Heritage Studies and Digital Technologies require curriculum and syllabus development and are not to be examined until 2028.
The page states that 2026 and 2027 candidates sit English Language and General Mathematics as the two currently available core subjects, alongside selected other subjects.

The official 2026–2027 entry notice groups subject choices into Science, Humanities, Business and Trade subject families, with examples including Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Further Mathematics, Geography, Government, Accounting, Commerce, Economics and vocational subjects.
sources.limits: Nigeria-specific and cohort/year-dependent; do not generalise to every WAEC member country.

sources.title: NECO SSCE Internal
sources.summary: Official NECO information for the internal senior school certificate examination.
verified_notes: NECO describes SSCE Internal as the examination for candidates in their final year of Senior Secondary School Education.
The page describes compulsory cross-cutting subjects and additional subjects based on specialisation, within the stated overall subject-count range.
sources.limits: Dates, fees and subject counts are session-specific. Read current-year guidelines.

sources.title: NECO SSCE External
sources.summary: Official NECO information for external/private candidates.
verified_notes: NECO describes SSCE External as an examination for candidates who are not in the school system.
The 2026 notice describes dual mode with computer-based and pen-and-paper options; candidates must consult the current session guidelines.
sources.limits: Mode, procedure, fees and dates are session-specific.

sources.title: Assessment and exams — Diploma Programme

verified_notes: The IB describes both external and internal assessment in the Diploma Programme.
The IB lists examinations, essays, structured problems, data-response tasks and other formats; internal-assessment examples include oral work, fieldwork, laboratory work and investigations.
sources.limits: Not a complete subject guide or diploma-award rulebook.

sources.title: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus 2027–2029
sources.summary: Official subject syllabus for Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618, applicable to June and November examinations in 2027, 2028 and 2029.
verified_notes: The document identifies syllabus code 9618 and states that it applies to examinations in 2027, 2028 and 2029, with June and November series available.
The syllabus contents include AS and A Level subject content, assessment overview, assessment objectives, assessment details and submission of Paper 4 Practical.

The stated aims include computational thinking, principles of solving problems using computers, computer-system components and their interrelationships, networks and the internet, and developing computer-based solutions.
The syllabus identifies computational thinking, programming paradigms, communication, computer architecture and hardware, and data representation and structures as key concepts.
sources.limits: This record covers Cambridge 9618 only and the stated 2027–2029 version. It is not a grade-threshold table, and it must not be applied to IGCSE, other A Level subjects, 2026 exams or another exam board.

sources.qualification: International Advanced Subsidiary and International Advanced Level Computer Science (XCP01/YCP01)
sources.title: Pearson Edexcel International Advanced Level Computer Science specification, Issue 1, March 2026
sources.summary: Official Pearson Edexcel specification for the new International AS and A Level Computer Science qualification, first taught September 2026.
verified_notes: The specification identifies XCP01 as International Advanced Subsidiary and YCP01 as International Advanced Level Computer Science; it is Issue 1, March 2026.
The qualification is first taught in September 2026 and first examined in June 2027.

The four units are Unit 1 Principles of Computer Science, Unit 2 Practical Programming and Problem-solving, Unit 3 Advanced Principles of Computer Science, and Unit 4 Advanced Practical Programming and Problem-solving.
The specification describes Unit 1 and Unit 3 as written or onscreen assessment options, while Unit 2 and Unit 4 are practical programming examinations delivered onscreen.
The subject develops programming skills using Python 3 and includes computational thinking, algorithms, data representation, computer systems, networks, cybersecurity and data handling.
The qualification overview states that the four units are equally weighted and externally assessed; IAS consists of Units 1 and 2, while IAL requires all four units.
sources.limits: This is the new Pearson Edexcel International AS/A Level Computer Science specification, not legacy International A Level subjects or Cambridge 9618. First examination timing and unit codes must be matched to the learner's qualification and series. Do not infer grade boundaries from this specification.

sources.title: FBISE notification: revised Scheme of Studies 2024, November 2026
sources.summary: Official FBISE notification dated 16 November 2026 concerning an update to the 2024 Scheme of Studies and bilingual SSC papers from First Annual Examination 2027.
verified_notes: The notification is dated 16 November 2026 and refers to an updated or revised Scheme of Studies 2024.

It states that FBISE SSC examination papers in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry and Biology or Computer Science will be administered bilingually in Urdu and English from First Annual Examination 2027 onwards.
The notification directs readers to the FBISE website for the updated Scheme of Studies 2024.
sources.limits: This is a policy notification about specified SSC subjects and language of papers, not the full subject curriculum or HSSC syllabus. Confirm the exact class, subject, scheme and current model paper before giving detailed syllabus advice.

sources.title: IB Diploma Programme assessment and exams
sources.summary: Official IB overview of Diploma Programme assessment, describing external examinations and internal assessment across DP courses.
verified_notes: The IB describes DP assessment as direct evidence of achievement against the stated goals of DP courses.

The assessment overview describes external examinations and internal assessment; examples of internal assessment include oral work, fieldwork, laboratory work, mathematical investigations and artistic performances.
The IB states that DP results are determined against set standards rather than each student's rank relative to other candidates.
sources.limits: This is a programme-level assessment overview, not an individual DP subject guide, grade-boundary table or complete diploma-award regulation. Subject-specific requirements must be checked separately.
